record.title: 245 Eglinton Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application- Decision Report - Approval
trackingStatus: City Council adopted this item on July 29 and 30, 2026 with amendments.
This item was considered by North York Community Council on July 7, 2026. It is being forwarded to City Council without recommendations. It will be considered by City Council on July 29 and 30, 2026.

sections.heading: Community Council Recommendations
paragraphs: North York Community Council:
1. Forwarded this item to City Council without recommendation.

sections.heading: Decision Advice and Other Information
paragraphs: The North York Community Council held a statutory public meeting on July 7, 2026, and notice was given in accordance with the Planning Act, RSO 1990.

sections.heading: Origin
paragraphs: (June 8, 2026) Report from the Director, Community Planning, North York District

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: This Report recommends approval of the application to amend the Official Plan and Zoning By-law for a mixed use building consisting of two, 59-storey towers on a connected 3 and 4-storey base, with retail at grade at 245 Eglinton Avenue East. The towers would have heights of approximately 190 metres each, plus 6 metre mechanical penthouses.

The total gross floor area (GFA) of the proposal is 82,742 square metres, with a resulting Floor Space Index (FSI) of 17.2 times the lot area. The proposal includes 2,802 square metres of retail uses at grade, 1,202 residential dwelling units, and a total of 4,837 square metres of amenity space (indoor and outdoor amenity combined).

trackingStatus: City Council adopted this item on July 29 and 30, 2026 with amendments.
This item was considered by Toronto and East York Community Council on July 8 and 9, 2026 and was adopted with amendments. It will be considered by City Council on July 29 and 30, 2026.

meta.Wards: 4 - Parkdale - High Park, 9 - Davenport, 10 - Spadina - Fort York, 13 - Toronto Centre

sections.heading: Community Council Recommendations
paragraphs: The Toronto and East York Community Council recommends that:

1. City Council request the General Manager, Transportation Services, in collaboration with the Chief Executive Officer, Toronto Transit Commission, to investigate the feasibility and options for expanding Transit Priority Measures for the 505 Dundas streetcar outside of the currently implemented Transit Priority Measures, to further reduce travel times and improve reliability of the Dundas streetcar for transit riders; such investigation to include further analysis of the 505 Dundas streetcar performance and development of an engagement plan to support future Transit Priority Measures.

2. City Council request the General Manager, Transportation Services, in collaboration with the Chief Executive Officer, Toronto Transit Commission, to report back with recommendations on Part 1 above in the first quarter of 2027.

sections.heading: Origin
paragraphs: (June 19, 2026) Report from the Director, Congestion and Network Management, Transportation Services

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: In December 2025, Transportation Services recommended permanent parking and traffic amendments to Dundas Street East and West to enhance transit service as part of 2025.TE27.51 Transit Priority Measures to Support the 505 Dundas 6-Minute Network. The transit priority measures (TPMs) implemented included expanding �No Stopping� coverage of the AM and PM peak periods on weekdays, as well as new and expanded left-turn restrictions.

These changes were in support of 6-minute headways on the 505 Dundas streetcar route from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. daily, which began on November 15, 2026. The goal of the TPMs is to help improve the speed and reliability of the 505 Dundas route and minimize the risk of increased bunching and gapping associated with moving to a more frequent headway.

record.title: 1337 Queen Street West - Demolition and New Construction on a Designated Heritage Property under Part V, Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval
trackingStatus: This item will be considered by Toronto Preservation Board on November 16, 2026.

sections.heading: Origin
paragraphs: (October 28, 2026) Report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning

sections.heading: Recommendations
paragraphs: The Senior Manager, Heritage Planning, Urban Design, City Planning recommends that:

1. City Council approve the demolition of the non-contributing building and the erection of a new 16-storey mixed-use building at 1337 Queen Street West, in the Parkdale Main Street Heritage Conservation District in accordance with subsections 42(1) 4 and 42(1) 2 of the Ontario Heritage Act, and subject to the following conditions:

a. that the replacement building for 1337 Queen Street West is constructed substantially in accordance with the plans and elevations prepared by LGA Architectural Partners dated September 25, 2026, on file with the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning.

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: This report recommends that City Council approve the demolition of an existing building on a non-contributing property located at 1337 Queen Street West within the Parkdale Main Street Heritage Conservation District (PHCD) and approve the erection of a replacement building in accordance with Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act in connection with the City-led Parkdale Hub project.

The proposed development is for the West Block of the Parkdale Hub project to erect a new 16-storey mixed-use tower with a 4-storey podium building that will include purpose-built affordable housing; and which will remain under ownership of the City.

A heritage permit for the project was previously approved on June 24 and 25, 2026, by City Council. The current proposal is largely the same as the previous approval, but a change has been made to the height of the podium of the new building. The street wall height of the new podium building has been increased by 1.2m which means that it no longer matches the height of the adjacent contributing building at 1347 Queen Street West. It also does not include the 5.0m step back required by the PHCD Plan for any parts of the new building that are taller than the adjacent contributing property. Consequently, a new Section 42 approval under the Ontario Heritage Act is required.

One of the objectives of the PHCD Plan is to conserve the consistent and continuous streetwall that characterises most of the PHCD but this section of south side of Queen Street West has neither a consistent nor a continuous street wall. Therefore, the proposed modest height increase for the podium of the new Parkdale Hub West Block development would not harm the character or appearance of the District or be contrary to the objectives of the PHCD Plan. As such staff have no concern with the lack of a step back of the top of the new podium building in this location.

sections.heading: Financial Impact
paragraphs: There are no financial implications resulting from the recommendations included in this report in the current budget year or in future years.
The Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer has reviewed this report and agrees with the information as presented in the Financial Impact Section.

citations.quote: it no longer matches the height of the adjacent contributing building at 1347 Queen Street West
citations.sourceLabel: City of Toronto item page 2027.PB1.6

whoIsAffected.text: People walking in the area: the design includes a walking route between Dunn Avenue and Masaryk Park.

citations.quote: an east-west pedestrian connection between Dunn Avenue and Masaryk Park
citations.sourceLabel: Staff report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning

whoIsAffected.text: City budget: staff say this recommendation has no cost to the City budget this year or in future years.

citations.quote: There are no financial implications resulting from the recommendations included in this report in the current budget year or in future years.
citations.sourceLabel: City of Toronto item page 2027.PB1.6

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Condition: the new building must be built substantially as shown in the architect's plans dated September 25, 2026.

citations.quote: constructed substantially in accordance with the plans and elevations prepared by LGA Architectural Partners dated September 25, 2026
citations.sourceLabel: City of Toronto item page 2027.PB1.6

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: A separate minor variance application is also needed for this change.
conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: The record does not say when that application will be decided or how to comment on it.

citations.quote: A separate minor variance application is also required for the proposed revisions.
citations.sourceLabel: Staff report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Under the heritage district plan, demolition cannot start until City Council has approved the plans for the replacement building and a heritage permit has been issued.

citations.quote: demolition activity shall not begin until plans for the replacement building(s) or structure(s) have been submitted and approved by Toronto City Council, and a heritage permit issued by the City
citations.sourceLabel: Staff report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning

staff.text: Staff recommend approval, with one condition about following the architect's plans.

citations.quote: It is therefore recommended that City Council approve the application under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
citations.sourceLabel: Staff report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning

whatHappensNext.text: The Toronto Preservation Board will consider this item on November 16, 2026.

citations.quote: This item will be considered by Toronto Preservation Board on November 16, 2026.
citations.sourceLabel: City of Toronto item page 2027.PB1.6

whatHappensNext.text: The staff report is also addressed to Toronto and East York Community Council, and it asks City Council to make the final decision.
whatHappensNext.caveat: The City's item page does not yet list dates for those later steps.

citations.quote: Toronto and East York Community Council
citations.sourceLabel: Staff report from the Senior Manager, Heritage Planning
